subject: Life Skills
title: Tipping Around the World
description: A quick, practical guide to Tipping Around the World.

hook.text: In Japan, leaving a tip can offend your server. In the US, skipping one can ruin their paycheck.

buildup.text: Tipping started in 17th-century English pubs. Patrons slipped coins 'To Insure Promptness' — T.I.P.

discovery.text: In the US, servers earn below minimum wage and rely on 15–20% tips. The system bakes gratuity into pay.

twist.text: In Australia, wages are high and tipping is rare. Leaving cash feels generous, not obligatory.

climax.text: Before traveling, search 'tipping norms in [country].' Five minutes of research prevents real awkwardness.

punchline.text: Generosity means knowing the local rules first.

quiz.question: Why can tipping be offensive in Japan?
options: It implies the server needs charity
Good service is expected as standard, not extra
Japanese currency does not support small amounts
